chunks: On the twenty-ninth of Dhu al-Qa'dah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Ka'bah, and it was the first mercy that descended. So whoever performs sawm (fasting) on that day, it is an expiation for seventy years.

key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhu al-Qa'dah, the sacred lunar month mentioned as the date of this event
key_terms.رَحْمَةٍ: mercy, described here as the first mercy to descend
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ سَنَةً: seventy years, expressing the magnitude of the reward
key_terms.كَفَّارَةَ: expiation; that which wipes away sins

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on the twenty-ninth of Dhu al-Qa'dah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Ka'bah was sent down on the twenty-ninth of Dhu al-Qa'dah and describes it as the first mercy to descend. It also mentions the great reward of sawm (fasting) on that day, namely expiation for seventy years.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "On the 29th of Dhu al-Qa‘dah, Allah (swt), the Almighty, sent down the Ka‘bah, which was the first mercy to descend. Whoever fasts on that day, it will be an expiation for seventy years."
